title: Totals that multiply, skip and reconcile

docs.syntax: =SUMPRODUCT(pairs) values a table; =SUBTOTAL(9,range) adds a group; a ratio of the two is a weighted figure
docs.explain:
The sheet carries two routes to the same number. Column D already holds each row's price times its quantity, and the total under it adds those three lines to 100. SUMPRODUCT rebuilds the same 100 from the prices in B2:B4 and the quantities in C2:C4.

Divide one route by the other and the answer is 1. That is the check: a line typed over, or a row added after the fact, moves the ratio away from 1 while both formulas still return a number. Rounding to one decimal place makes any drift visible at a glance.

Each function starts from a different place on the sheet. SUMPRODUCT walks two ranges in step and multiplies the pairs. SUBTOTAL and AGGREGATE walk a single range, with a function number choosing the calculation, and AGGREGATE adds an options number for what to skip.

errors.text: The subtotal under the line column is zero, so there is nothing to divide by.
The two ranges in SUMPRODUCT are a different height, so the pairs cannot form.
A line value was typed over, so the two routes disagree and the ratio drifts away from 1.

docs.atWork: Checking that a line total agrees with the prices and quantities behind it.
docs.outcome: Reconcile two routes to the same total and read the ratio as a pass or a fail.
docs.teaches: SUBTOTAL over a value column and a SUMPRODUCT that reproduces it
docs.dataset: Stock list with a value column and a total row to check

screens.prompt: In D5, total the Line column with SUBTOTAL.

hints.syntax: =SUBTOTAL(9,D2:D4): the number comes first, then the line column.
hints.func-subtotal: The total under a table that may be filtered is a SUBTOTAL, with 9 for SUM.
hints.value: Twenty plus twenty plus sixty is 100.
hints.error: Dividing the line total by zero gives #DIV/0! in place of 100.

reject.why: a plain SUM keeps adding rows a filter has hidden
the last line value is left out
function number four returns the largest line, not the total
the range starts one row late
the total is divided by zero
the range sits outside the parentheses

screens.prompt: In D5, divide the price-times-quantity total by the line total and round it to one decimal place.

hints.syntax: =ROUND(SUMPRODUCT(B2:B4,C2:C4)/SUBTOTAL(9,D2:D4),1): the ratio sits inside the ROUND.
hints.func-sumproduct: The numerator is price times quantity across the rows, which is what SUMPRODUCT does.
hints.func-subtotal: The denominator is the total under the line column, and that total is a SUBTOTAL.
hints.require-ref: Both routes read the table rows instead of numbers typed by hand.
hints.value: 100 divided by 100 is 1, so the two routes agree.
hints.error: A zero in the denominator gives #DIV/0!, and the ratio never reaches the screen.

reject.why: neither route is written: the prices are averaged on their own
the denominator is a plain sum rather than the subtotal under the column
the quantity total is 9, so the ratio is nowhere near one
the last line value is missing from the denominator
the first item is missing from the numerator
the ratio is then divided by zero
the ratio falls outside the parentheses ROUND needs

seo.title: Reconcile a stock sheet in Excel
seo.description: Total the value column with SUBTOTAL, then rebuild it from prices and quantities with SUMPRODUCT. A ratio of exactly one means both routes agree.
